findings: The split preserves actual Intel Darwin host, exact producer Xcode and Simulator SDK, actual bundle identifier/platform/SDK/deployment metadata, actual Mach-O x86_64 architecture, and strict deep signature verification. These immutable checks run before Simulator create/boot in the recovery helper.

After bootstatus, the helper still reads the available runtime list, requires the original available runtime/version, reads current devices, and requires exactly the selected UDID in Booted state under that runtime. No guest uname is used.

Each compatibility command keeps its existing30-second limit; create/boot and bootstatus keep120/300-second limits. Existing setup timeout/error evidence and owned-process cleanup remain. The change does not increase a test or metadata deadline.

The actual app binary digest is checked again immediately before installation, so a file change after immutable verification fails closed. Source/runner/manifest/binary binding, original cases, per-case outcomes and final binary checks remain.

The combined verify_compatibility API still executes both phases for existing callers. The running d46 normal consumer invokes that combined API after boot; this recovery-only ordering correction does not retroactively change the current run.

verification.countRule: The22 nested Python checks are contained in one of the4 formal cases; do not add them to the formal total.
verification.meaningfulChecks: Executed extracted actual main setup statements in order:5 immutable reads, create/boot/bootstatus,2 live runtime/device reads, binary recheck/install. A changed pre-install app digest rejects installation. Existing wrong-host/bundle/toolchain/runtime, timeout, extraction, trace and owned-child limits remain covered.

limits: Local commands controlling macOS metadata and Simulator responses are doubles; this is not an actual macOS, Simulator, launch or85-case acceptance.
The ordering repair addresses a demonstrated setup-risk boundary, not a proven cause of the observed postboot SDK command delay. It may still fail honestly on a future host/tool error.
No reader, product runtime, native library, binary bytes, signature, build, source ref or provider data was changed by this review.

Reusing a future d46 producer artifact requires an explicitly reviewed immutable d46 source/tree/runner/manifest/app-digest binding; the current recovery helper remains bound to the older b568 binary.
